# Frozen synthetic extraction corpus

SW-28 / STD D09 and S09: 30 academic documents, ten each of Form 137, NCAE and
NAT. Each category has two clean, two low-quality, two missing-field, two
non-standard and two mixed-quality cases. These are synthetic document facsimiles,
not official DepEd templates or evidence of representative school scan quality.
Grade 10 and SHS counseling remain the scope. No real student's data is included.

The committed manifest declares category, condition, actual format/MIME, page
count, SHA-256, visible source lines and field-level answer keys. JPEG, PNG, WEBP
and scanned PDF inputs are represented. Low-quality images have reduced resolution,
blur, rotation and compression; mixed-quality images alternate contrast. Mixed
PDFs have two pages. Non-standard cases reverse the academic field order.
Missing-field cases include blank labeled scores and omitted overall/text values.
Zero is a legitimate score. Form 137 includes distracting quarterly values and
printed final ratings; the score uses the printed final values only.

Names, birthdates and IDs are conspicuously fictitious markers. Their presence
in approved extraction pixels is permitted by the SW-05 waiver. This corpus must
never be described as a successful local-redaction test.

The system uses answer keys authored from the synthetic source values independently of provider responses. Human answer-key verification passes. The committed manifest hash freezes the reviewed corpus. The system retains the corpus unchanged during scored runs.

Scoring freezes these rules: exact numbers (no numeric tolerance), case/whitespace
normalization for labels, no aliases or inferred values, and explicit null for
blank/absent values. Form 137 rows match subject + grade level + school year;
row order and generated UUIDs are irrelevant. Duplicate or invented rows increase
the denominator; omitted fields never count as correct nulls. Every document attempt retains every expected field in the denominator. All thirty inputs contribute
before counselor edits. Scalar totals and row identity/grade observations are
eligible; synthetic identifiers and quarterly distractors are excluded. These
rules are versioned in `scripts/extraction/score.ts` and its source hash in reports.

`node scripts/extraction/generate-fixtures.mjs` is a maintainer utility, not part
of tests/CI. It requires a new corpus version and review if used after scoring.
Font/runtime differences may change generated bytes; committed hashes define the
actual corpus. Never regenerate during a live evaluation.
